quick-headline.why: The JD's core stack line is 'Python, Web APIs, SDKs, GenAI, LLMs and RAG' and the Role Overview opens 'an elite Python engineer'. The master headline led with Java + Spring Boot and did not contain the word Python, so a keyword screen at Andela or Wolters Kluwer returned zero hits on the first word of the stack. Python (FastAPI, LangChain, LangGraph, MCP) and RAG + LLM now sit in positions three and four; Java + Spring Boot moved back but did not move off. Neptune was dropped to hold the length near the master's; GNN, HIPAA and ISO 27001 all stay.
quick-headline.heads_up: Tagline exception applies - MCP, RAG, LLM, AWS, GNN and HIPAA are deliberately unexpanded here and every one of them is expanded on first use in the Summary or the skills blocks that follow. Length is 199 characters against the master's 195, so it will not truncate any differently than the master already does.
quick-headline.hygiene: Headline only - no bullet rules apply.

quick-summary.why: Rewritten to lead with the Python / AI-platform stack instead of Java, and to put the Claude Code and OpenAI Codex rollout in sentence two. That rollout is a REQUIRED line on both JD bars ('Daily use of AI coding assistants ... with concrete examples of productivity gains, guardrails and rollout to other engineers') and is the one criterion where he is likely to beat every other candidate in the pipeline. Java is not deleted - it is the fourth sentence, still at 11 years across three eras, still carrying the regulated-banking multi-tenancy and the zero-disruption SSO migration.
quick-summary.heads_up: No new claim anywhere. Python, FastAPI, LangChain and LangGraph all come from professional-journey.md line 678. The 25-30% infrastructure cost and the under-10-minute deploy time are the two user-confirmed metrics from 2026-08-25. 'A measured rollout with hands-on review as the guardrail' is the journey doc's own wording ('all under hands-on review'). Azure is not mentioned - it is a never-claim item and the JD only prefers it.
quick-summary.hygiene: First-use expansions all live here in reading order: web application programming interfaces (APIs), Model Context Protocol (MCP), artificial intelligence (AI), Amazon Web Services (AWS), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), large language model (LLM), software as a service (SaaS), single sign-on (SSO). Django and Model Context Protocol servers come from CLAUDE.md's user-confirmed safe-to-claim list; Pydantic v2, Ollama, golden fixtures and Normalised Discounted Cumulative Gain are verified in killer-query-case-studies/; Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform are user-confirmed 2026-08-25. quick-skills-bd.hygiene: Six lines. HIPAA, B2B and WCAG are each expanded at first use here (HIPAA's earlier appearance is in the headline, which carries the tagline exception).

(1) 'Assembled' now names Python, FastAPI, LangChain and LangGraph - straight from professional-journey.md line 678, adding no claim, and this is the single highest-value change in the file. (2) 'Secured' gained Amazon SageMaker and Ollama, both already in the master's own skills block and in the case studies. (3) 'Provisioned' gained Docker and lost one awkward preposition. quick-vp.hygiene: 7 bullets, 19-24 words each, unique leading verbs across all ten roles, at least one number and one raw <strong> in every one, no trailing periods. Dropping the Datadog bullet removed one 'cutting' echo of the Teletext leading verb 'Cut'. Known root echoes carried over from the master and NOT introduced here: 'first-cut implementation' in the Drove bullet echoes 'Implemented' leading a Deque bullet, and 'Security' in the Business & Delivery block echoes 'Secured'.

quick-deque.why: Grown from 6 bullets to 9, taken from #merged-deque, and reordered so the platform-services-consumed-by-other-teams evidence leads. That is the JD's 'Platform Architect: You design systems consumed by other engineering teams and reason clearly about compatibility, versioning ...' and the Principal bar's 'ownership of a platform, service family or SDK used by multiple engineering teams'. Bullets one to three - the central authentication service, the billing service consumed by every product, and the shared platform APIs to 20+ enterprise clients with API versioning and backward compatibility - are the closest honest analogue he has to the SDK requirement. Modernised (GitHub Actions) and Slashed (Puppeteer regression framework) were pulled forward from the eight unmerged card bullets because the JD names GitHub Actions and automated testing explicitly. Orchestrated (axe-core scanning) and Accelerated (time-to-market) were left out.
quick-deque.heads_up: One in-place edit: 'Forged' traded 'in Java and Spring Boot' for 'on OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0'. That is a deliberate trade - OAuth2/OIDC is a stated JD requirement, and Java + Spring Boot still appears in three other Deque bullets and in the skills block. The 70-80% consolidation figure and 'approximately 300 enterprise instances' are both on the confirm-or-reject list; they are carried exactly as the master and the merge proposal word them and were not touched. ISO 27001 here is Deque's certification and is a DIFFERENT thing from the HIPAA certification driver on the VoltusWave chat platform - be ready to say so out loud if an interviewer merges them.
quick-deque.hygiene: 9 bullets, 15-25 words each. JWT is used short here because it is expanded in the Engineering Excellence block, which comes first in reading order; same for CI/CD. 'cutting backups' in the Stewarded bullet is a known echo of the Teletext leading verb 'Cut' - it carries that migration's only two hard numbers, so the word cannot go without the metrics going.
